pixel_observations.description: Circular color endoscopic field against black borders; pink tissue with branching red fine vessels and varying illumination. No instrument in these sampled images.
An oval/circular dark opening and nearby translucent reflective bubbles appear in a raised pink tissue area; view orientation changes. No independent anatomical laterality inferred.
A pale tubular instrument extends from the left toward the opening, with its tip close to the tissue.
Pink vascular tissue fills the sampled field with changing framing and the prior pale instrument no longer visible.
A long dark reflective shaft crosses from the lower edge toward a small tissue opening near the upper-middle; the instrument/tissue orientation changes through the sampled sequence.

A second pale instrument enters from the upper-right edge alongside the dark diagonal shaft, contacting tissue near its upper tip. Visible contact is described without inferring injected volume or exact onset/completion.
Closer, brightly illuminated orange/pink tissue forms a pale rounded mound-like profile next to a darker slit; portions are soft/blurred and instrument profiles are partly at the edge.
Wider circular field again shows pink tissue and branching red vessels around a brighter central raised-looking area; no clearly visible instrument in these final sampled frames.

author_context.subject: patient

evidence.quote: Two years and six months after kidney transplantation, she was admitted for endoscopic correction of vesicoureteral reflux. Under spinal anesthesia, cystoscopy was performed, and the transplant ureteral orifice was identified on the anterior bladder wall, slightly to the right side. The ureteral orifice appeared mildly dilated. A ureteral stent was temporarily inserted to adjust the position and alignment of the intramural portion of the transplant ureter, thereby facilitating submucosal injection using a metallic injection needle. Subsequently, a dextranomer/hyaluronic acid copolymer (Deflux) was injected submucosally beneath the transplanted ureteral orifice according to the double-HIT technique (Video 1) [], with a total volume of 2 mL injected.

Endoscopic subureteric Deflux injection for vesicoureteral reflux
